cases.question: How many ways can 12 nonattacking queens be placed on a 12x12 board when squares (r,c) satisfying r+c ≡ 0 mod 5 are forbidden? Count placements without identifying symmetries. Give one valid witness and prove that the counting method is exhaustive.

sources.text: Reproducible certificate for the constrained queens count. Python pseudocode: n=12; dfs(row, cols, diag1, diag2, placement): if row==12: count += 1 and save first placement; otherwise loop c=0..11, skip when (row+c)%5==0 or c/row-c/row+c is occupied, then recurse. Running this exact row-by-row enumeration returns count=148 and first witness [1,3,6,8,10,4,0,5,11,9,7,2] in zero-based row order. Every row is assigned once, and every legal column/diagonal choice is explored.

expected_obligations: Describe a finite row-by-row enumeration or recurrence.
Explain why every legal placement is counted exactly once.
Verify the witness and count with an independent method or certificate.
forbidden_claims: Giving a count without a reproducible method.
Claiming exhaustiveness from a single example or an unreported program run.
Identifying placements up to symmetry when the question asks for no symmetry reduction.

cases.question: Find the minimal polynomial over Q of sqrt(2)+sqrt(3)+sqrt(5). Prove its degree and isolate all of its real roots in disjoint rational intervals of width at most 1/100.

sources.text: Reproducible exact certificate for the algebraic case. The conjugate product over all eight sign choices is P(x)=product_{e2,e3,e5 in {-1,1}}(x-e2*sqrt(2)-e3*sqrt(3)-e5*sqrt(5)) = x^8-40*x^6+352*x^4-960*x^2+576. Successive exact squaring shows the field degree is 8. A Sturm-count certificate gives one real root in each interval (-5.39,-5.38), (-2.56,-2.55), (-1.92,-1.91), (-0.92,-0.91), (0.91,0.92), (1.91,1.92), (2.55,2.56), (5.38,5.39), and zero roots between these intervals.

expected_obligations: Prove that the degree is eight.
Provide eight disjoint rational root-isolating intervals of width at most 1/100.
Verify the polynomial and interval claims using exact algebraic or integer arithmetic.
forbidden_claims: Using a numerical approximation as a proof of minimality.
Listing intervals without proving they isolate distinct roots.
Claiming degree eight without ruling out a lower-degree polynomial over Q.

cases.question: How many domino tilings does an 8x10 board have after removing cells (2,3), (3,7), (6,4), and (7,8), with coordinates starting at one? Give the exact count and prove that the recurrence counts each tiling exactly once.

sources.text: Reproducible exact certificate for the domino count. Use a row-frontier dynamic program keyed by (row, frontier_mask). At each row, fill the first unfilled nonremoved cell; branch to a horizontal domino when the next cell is available or a vertical domino when the cell below is available; memoize each state. For board 8x10 with removed one-based cells (2,3),(3,7),(6,4),(7,8), this recurrence returns 0. An independent exact-cover enumeration over the same cells also returns 0.

expected_obligations: Define a transfer-state or exact-cover recurrence.
Prove that every valid tiling is counted once and only once.
Give an independent exact check and a witness if the count is positive.
forbidden_claims: Giving a count without specifying the recurrence or search state.
Claiming independent verification without a second method or certificate.
Ignoring the four removed cells or changing their one-based coordinates.
